practiceNotes: This is a proposed curriculum. Enrollment, equipment access, authorization and successful assessment are not assumed.

Use spaced retrieval for definitions, model assumptions, representations, diagnostic distinctions and method selection. Require separate graded proofs, calculations, code, laboratory records and extended investigations.

Interleave new work with delayed transfer tasks and cumulative assessments. A correct recalled formula does not substitute for choosing assumptions, checking units, diagnosing failure or validating results.

Wet laboratories require trained supervision, institutional risk assessment, appropriate containment, chemical hygiene, waste handling and approved emergency procedures. Use benign substitutes or supplied datasets where facilities are unavailable.

Human-participant, animal, environmental and genomic-data work requires applicable consent, ethics review, permits, privacy safeguards and community governance. Case-based ethical assessment remains part of the teaching contracts.
Security work is restricted to owned or explicitly authorized isolated systems. Robotics, high voltage, lasers, radiation, pressure systems and cryogenics require suitable facilities and supervision.

Provided software may be used only where a contract teaches its inputs, assumptions, diagnostics and interpretation. Tasks specifying implementation or derivation must assess those performances directly.
Maintain reproducible computational environments, versioned data and provenance. Assess uncertainty, negative results and model mismatch rather than rewarding only expected conclusions.

outcomes.description: Compute fundamental groups using coverings and van Kampen constructions.
Construct chain complexes and calculate simplicial or cellular homology with exact sequences.
Prove non-equivalence and extension obstructions using functoriality and homotopy invariance.

practice: Compute invariants of explicit cell complexes and write obstruction proofs.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.description: Formal mathematical reasoning and its limits.
decks.title: Mathematical Logic

outcomes.description: Construct formal derivations and models and prove soundness for a specified first-order calculus.
Prove a completeness construction and use compactness to build or exclude models.
Explain and reconstruct arithmetization and diagonal arguments underlying incompleteness under precise hypotheses.

practice: Write formal derivations, construct models and trace a diagonalization proof.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Dynamical Systems

outcomes.description: Prove local stability and invariant-set results using linearization and Lyapunov functions.
Derive elementary normal forms and classify local bifurcations in parameterized systems.
Analyze symbolic dynamics, sensitive dependence and invariant measures in explicit maps.

practice: Prove stability and bifurcation claims and compare phase portraits with counterexamples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Geometry

outcomes.description: Construct affine schemes, structure sheaves and glued examples and compare morphisms with ring maps.
Compute divisors and line bundles on elementary curves and relate local data to global sections.

practice: Construct explicit schemes and line bundles; present a proof-based study of a curve.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: The Physical World

outcomes.description: Distinguish observation, model and approximation using scale, dimensions and limiting cases.
Explain motion, forces, energy transfer and thermal processes using diagrams and proportional reasoning.
Interpret elementary electric, magnetic, wave and atomic models and identify their limitations.

practice: Build qualitative predictions and energy diagrams; test simple motion, thermal and optical demonstrations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Physical Measurement

outcomes.description: Choose instruments, calibrate linear scales and distinguish resolution, repeatability and systematic error.
Report measured quantities using means, spreads, elementary propagated uncertainties and dimensionally consistent graphs.

practice: Calibrate a simple sensor and produce a reproducible measurement notebook with uncertainty budgets.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Newtonian Mechanics

outcomes.description: Construct vector force models and solve constrained elementary motion problems.
Apply work-energy and momentum balances to continuous forces, collisions and systems of particles.
Calculate rigid-body rotation, angular momentum and central gravitational trajectories in elementary cases.

practice: Solve free-body, collision and rotational problems; compare model predictions with supplied motion data.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Macroscopic thermal models with microscopic interpretation.
decks.title: Thermal Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate heat, work and internal-energy changes for specified thermodynamic processes.
Calculate entropy changes and engine limits and distinguish reversible from irreversible processes.
Relate ideal-gas pressure, temperature and transport scales to molecular averages.

practice: Analyze cycles and calorimetry data; derive elementary gas-pressure and mean-free-path estimates.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Waves and Optics

outcomes.description: Verify harmonic and traveling-wave solutions and calculate phase, energy flux and resonance.
Calculate interference and elementary diffraction patterns using superposition and aperture integration.
Trace paraxial optical systems and calculate polarization transformations in elementary configurations.

practice: Predict and measure fringe patterns, focal behavior and polarization with uncertainty-aware comparisons.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Electrical systems before advanced field theory.
decks.title: Circuits and Electronics

outcomes.description: Solve resistive, RC and RLC networks using Kirchhoff laws and initial-value models.
Calculate complex impedance, resonance and frequency response of elementary networks.
Analyze bounded diode and operational-amplifier models and measure signals without excessive loading.

practice: Build or emulate low-voltage circuits; compare transient and frequency-response measurements with models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electricity and Magnetism

outcomes.description: Calculate electric fields, potentials and capacitances using Coulomb and symmetric Gauss-law arguments.
Calculate magnetic forces and fields using Biot-Savart and symmetric Ampere-law arguments.
Calculate induced electromotive forces and electric and magnetic energy balances.

practice: Solve symmetric field problems and test induction predictions with supplied or measured traces.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive Euler-Lagrange equations, conserved quantities and constrained mechanical models.
Construct Hamiltonians and calculate canonical evolution, Poisson brackets and elementary canonical transformations.
Derive normal modes and stability of coupled mechanical systems.

practice: Derive competing formulations of constrained systems and solve normal-mode problems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Relativity through algebra and spacetime diagrams.
decks.title: Special Relativity

outcomes.description: Calculate Lorentz transformations and analyze simultaneity, proper time and causal intervals.
Solve relativistic collision and decay kinematics using energy-momentum invariants.

practice: Construct spacetime diagrams and solve invariant-mass and two-body kinematic problems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Foundations

outcomes.description: Calculate amplitudes, probabilities, expectation values and unitary evolution in finite-dimensional state spaces.
Solve elementary one-dimensional stationary wave equations and interpret tunneling and quantization.
Calculate spin measurements, tensor-product states and elementary entanglement correlations.

practice: Solve wells and barriers; calculate spin experiments and compare quantum with classical probability models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive angular-momentum coupling and solve central-potential quantum models.
Apply stationary and time-dependent perturbation, variational and semiclassical approximations with validity estimates.
Calculate elementary scattering amplitudes and cross sections using Born and partial-wave methods.
Construct symmetrized states and use occupation-number operators for identical particles.

practice: Derive hydrogenic states and transition rates; compare approximation methods on common benchmark Hamiltonians.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Classical Electrodynamics

outcomes.description: Solve Maxwell boundary-value problems using potentials, multipoles and Green-function constructions.
Derive retarded potentials and calculate elementary dipole radiation and radiated power.
Analyze waves, dispersion, reflection and energy flow in linear electromagnetic media.

practice: Derive fields and radiation for specified sources and compare boundary-condition and energy checks.

includes: Bose and Fermi statistics with local state-counting models

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Construct microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical ensembles and calculate thermodynamic observables.
Derive Bose and Fermi occupation laws from stated indistinguishable-state counting and analyze ideal gases.
Relate equilibrium fluctuations, susceptibilities and correlation functions in elementary models.

practice: Derive partition functions and compare ensemble predictions for spin, oscillator and gas models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Statistical Physics

outcomes.description: Derive mean-field phase behavior and analyze critical exponents and finite-size scaling.
Perform elementary real-space and momentum-shell coarse-graining and interpret fixed points.
Derive master-equation, kinetic and fluctuation-response descriptions near equilibrium.

practice: Analyze lattice models and derive scaling or response predictions with explicit approximation limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed-Matter Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate reciprocal lattices, diffraction conditions and phonon spectra in elementary crystal models.
Derive elementary Bloch and tight-binding bands and interpret carrier transport.
Analyze bounded models of magnetism, superconductivity and disorder and compare their experimental signatures.

practice: Calculate simple band and phonon structures and interpret diffraction, transport and phase-transition datasets.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Quantum structure and controlled optical interaction.
decks.title: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate fine and hyperfine structure and molecular rotational-vibrational levels using controlled approximations.
Derive two-level optical dynamics, transition rates and elementary laser and cooling models.
Infer level structure, line broadening and coupling parameters from resolved spectra.

practice: Derive spectral predictions and fit supplied line profiles using explicitly taught line-shape models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear Physics

outcomes.description: Use liquid-drop and shell models to estimate binding, stability and nuclear quantum numbers.
Calculate decay chains, reaction thresholds and elementary cross-section or barrier estimates.
Interpret radiation attenuation and detector spectra, distinguishing efficiency, resolution and background.

practice: Analyze supplied decay and detector data; calculate energetics and uncertainty-limited discrimination.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Particle Physics

outcomes.description: Use quantum numbers and discrete symmetries to classify particles and allowed reactions.
Calculate invariant masses, event yields and elementary significance measures from collider data.
Explain Standard Model interactions, symmetry breaking and neutrino evidence using bounded phenomenological models.

practice: Reconstruct supplied events and compare competing particle hypotheses without requiring QFT amplitude derivations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Fields describing flowing and deformable matter.
decks.title: Continuum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive mass, momentum and energy balances using stress tensors and constitutive assumptions.
Solve canonical viscous flows and use nondimensionalization, boundary layers and stability estimates.
Derive linear elastic response and wave propagation in simple solids and fluids.

practice: Derive pipe-flow and elastic-wave solutions and compare scaling predictions with supplied measurements.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Reusable control methods for physical systems.
decks.title: Control Systems

outcomes.description: Construct block-diagram, transfer-function and state-space models from specified dynamical equations.
Analyze closed-loop stability and design PID or lead-lag controllers with robustness margins.
Calculate controllability and observability and design elementary state-feedback and observer systems.

practice: Hand-design controllers and use a supplied control tool to test disturbances, saturation and model mismatch.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity

outcomes.description: Formulate stress-energy, covariant conservation and geodesic motion in Lorentzian geometry.
Derive and analyze elementary Einstein-equation solutions and their causal structure.
Calculate redshift, orbital corrections, lensing and linear gravitational-wave observables.

practice: Derive field and geodesic equations for symmetric metrics and calculate observable consequences.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory

outcomes.description: Quantize free scalar, spinor and gauge fields and construct propagators using canonical and path-integral methods.
Derive Feynman rules and calculate elementary scattering amplitudes and cross sections.
Regularize simple loop integrals and explain renormalization, gauge fixing and symmetry constraints.

practice: Derive propagators, compute tree amplitudes and carry a simple one-loop calculation through renormalization.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astronomy and Astrophysics

outcomes.description: Infer distances, luminosities, temperatures and velocities from calibrated photometric and spectral observations.
Construct elementary stellar structure, energy-generation and evolution models and compare planetary environments.
Use orbital and virial arguments to infer galactic masses and interpret missing-mass evidence.

practice: Analyze supplied spectra and catalogs; construct scaling-based stellar and orbital models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Cosmology

outcomes.description: Derive Friedmann dynamics and calculate cosmic distances and expansion histories.
Estimate freeze-out, nucleosynthesis and recombination using bounded reaction and equilibrium models.
Derive linear density growth and interpret background-radiation and large-scale-structure constraints.

practice: Calculate background histories and compare supplied cosmological observations with competing parameter choices.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Plasma Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate shielding, gyro-motion and ordering parameters and select particle, fluid or kinetic models.
Derive magnetohydrodynamic waves, equilibria and elementary stability criteria.
Linearize kinetic plasma equations and interpret collisionless damping and beam instabilities.

practice: Derive dispersion relations and compare plasma-model predictions across parameter regimes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics Methods

outcomes.description: Design calibrated sensor, amplification, filtering and acquisition chains with loading and bandwidth budgets.
Estimate noise spectra and apply averaging, lock-in detection and matched filtering to specified signals.
Design controls and uncertainty models that discriminate physical hypotheses and expose systematic error.

practice: Build or emulate an instrument chain and submit calibrated data, uncertainty analysis and a model-comparison report.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Numerical methods tied to physical structure.
decks.title: Computational Physics

outcomes.description: Implement Verlet and symplectic updates and compare long-time conservation with generic integrators.
Implement relaxation and finite-difference field solvers with physically correct sources and boundaries.
Separate discretization, finite-domain and model errors using convergence and conservation tests.

practice: Implement orbital and electrostatic solvers; publish reproducible convergence and invariant diagnostics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Many-Body Physics

outcomes.description: Construct many-body Green functions and derive elementary diagrammatic and response approximations.
Compare mean-field, correlation and effective descriptions of interacting phases against diagnostic observables.

practice: Reconstruct a many-body approximation and critically compare it with supplied numerical or experimental results.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Foundations

outcomes.description: Interpret formulas and calculate amount, mass, concentration and dilution using the mole concept.
Determine empirical composition and perform elementary atom and mass balances.
Read chemical measurements and report precision, units and basic uncertainty consistently.

practice: Solve composition and solution-preparation problems and document simulated balance and volumetric readings.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Atoms and Bonding

outcomes.description: Use bounded orbital and electron-configuration models to explain periodic trends and atomic spectra.
Construct Lewis, resonance and orbital-overlap models and predict molecular geometry and polarity.
Relate intermolecular forces to phase behavior, solubility and bulk properties.

practice: Compare alternative bonding representations and predict properties from unfamiliar molecular structures.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Reactions and Equilibrium

outcomes.description: Balance molecular and ionic reactions and calculate limiting reagents, yields and solution stoichiometry.
Solve equilibrium, buffer, titration and precipitation problems with justified approximations.
Balance redox reactions and interpret oxidation states and elementary electrochemical-cell potentials.

practice: Solve coupled mass-charge balances and compare predicted titration or precipitation behavior with data.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Methods

outcomes.description: Plan and execute weighing, solution preparation, titration, filtration, extraction and recrystallization.
Use hazard information to select controls, incompatible-material segregation and waste routes.
Maintain traceable observations, yield calculations and uncertainty-aware laboratory reports.

practice: Complete supervised benign preparations and separations with pre-lab risk assessments and auditable notebooks.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics

outcomes.description: Derive chemical potentials and thermodynamic identities from fundamental equations and Legendre transforms.
Calculate phase coexistence, mixing and phase-diagram constraints using chemical-potential equality.
Use activities, fugacities and standard states to calculate nonideal equilibria and temperature dependence.

practice: Derive equilibrium relations and calculate mixture and reaction equilibria from thermodynamic data.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics

outcomes.description: Determine reaction order and rate constants from concentration-time data and integrated laws.
Derive rate laws using elementary steps, pre-equilibrium and steady-state approximations.
Estimate activation parameters and distinguish kinetic, thermodynamic and catalytic effects.

practice: Hand-derive rate laws and use specified plotting procedures to discriminate mechanisms from supplied traces.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Structure

outcomes.description: Translate names, formulas and skeletal structures and identify functional groups and resonance relationships.
Assign stereochemical configurations and distinguish enantiomers, diastereomers and meso structures.
Construct conformational energy comparisons for chains and rings and predict favored conformers.

practice: Build molecular models and translate among projections, configurations and conformational diagrams.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms

outcomes.description: Predict substitution, elimination and addition outcomes using electron flow, energetics and stereochemistry.
Construct mechanisms for carbonyl, enolate and aromatic transformations and justify selectivity.
Predict radical-chain and elementary pericyclic products using locally developed orbital and conservation models.

practice: Write full mechanisms, isotope-label predictions and competing-pathway explanations for unfamiliar substrates.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis

outcomes.description: Design defensible multistep routes using disconnections, functional-group interconversions and accessible starting materials.
Choose order, protection and reaction conditions to control chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity.
Plan purification and analytical checks that distinguish desired products from plausible byproducts.

practice: Propose and critique complete routes; perform a supervised benign synthesis with spectral verification.

includes: Mechanistic and practical comparison of synthetic methods

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Synthetic Methods

outcomes.description: Design asymmetric routes using substrate, reagent and catalyst control and quantify selectivity relationships.
Evaluate synthetic methods using kinetics, scope, limitations, reproducibility and scale-dependent hazards.

practice: Reconstruct a literature synthesis and defend alternative stereocontrol and validation strategies.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry

outcomes.description: Explain main-group structures and reaction trends using bonding, oxidation states and periodicity.
Determine coordination geometry, isomerism and metal-ligand electron counts.
Use crystal- and ligand-field models to predict spin, color and elementary substitution behavior.

practice: Analyze unfamiliar complexes and compare structural, magnetic and reactivity evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organometallic Chemistry

outcomes.description: Predict oxidative addition, insertion, elimination and ligand-substitution steps using electron counting and structure.
Construct catalytic cycles and identify turnover, selectivity and catalyst-deactivation constraints.
Design kinetic, labeling and inhibition tests that discriminate organometallic mechanisms.

practice: Derive competing catalytic cycles and propose evidence capable of falsifying each.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry

outcomes.description: Design representative sampling and calculate univariate calibration, standard addition and recovery estimates.
Select and calculate gravimetric, titrimetric and equilibrium-based assays with interference checks.
Evaluate blanks, detection limits, precision, bias and fitness for an analytical decision.

practice: Validate a benign assay using standards, blanks and replicates; submit a defensible concentration report.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Spectroscopy

outcomes.description: Use locally specified energy-frequency, vibrational and electronic-transition models to interpret optical spectra.
Interpret chemical shifts, integrals, scalar splitting and elementary two-dimensional NMR correlations.
Combine formula, IR, UV-visible and NMR evidence to discriminate candidate molecular structures.

practice: Solve unknown-structure datasets and explicitly identify unresolved structural ambiguities.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Instrumental Analysis

outcomes.description: Calculate retention, resolution and plate performance and select chromatographic separation conditions.
Interpret ionization, mass analysis, isotope patterns and fragmentation for identification and quantitation.
Design coupled instrumental methods with calibration, matrix-effect and robustness validation.

practice: Optimize supplied chromatograms and mass spectra; produce a complete method-validation plan.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry

outcomes.description: Construct molecular orbitals using symmetry-adapted combinations and solve elementary secular equations.
Derive variational, Hartree-Fock and bounded density-functional formulations and explain correlation and basis errors.
Derive elementary rotational, vibrational and electronic spectral predictions and selection rules.

practice: Derive small-basis molecular models and compare predicted bonding and spectra with observations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Statistical Thermodynamics

outcomes.description: Construct translational, rotational, vibrational and electronic partition functions with symmetry corrections.
Derive molecular free energies and equilibrium constants with consistent standard states.
Analyze lattice, virial and elementary solvation models and diagnose their nonideality limitations.

practice: Calculate thermochemical properties from molecular data and compare ideal and interacting models.

includes: Charge transfer and bounded transport models

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Chemical transformations coupled to charge transport.
decks.title: Electrochemistry

outcomes.description: Derive electrode potentials and analyze reference electrodes, activities and electrochemical equilibria.
Derive Butler-Volmer limits and interpret voltammetry using locally developed diffusion and equivalent-circuit models.
Compare batteries, fuel cells and corrosion systems using efficiency, degradation and materials constraints.

practice: Interpret supplied voltammograms and impedance traces; calculate device losses and distinguish transport from kinetic limits.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Chemistry of interfaces and dispersed matter.
decks.title: Surface and Colloid Chemistry

outcomes.description: Calculate capillarity, wetting and surface-excess relationships from interfacial thermodynamics.
Derive and compare adsorption models and infer surface parameters from isotherms.
Use bounded double-layer and interaction-potential models to predict aggregation and colloidal stability.

practice: Analyze adsorption and aggregation datasets and design discriminating surface measurements.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Chemical synthesis and characterization of macromolecules.
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry

outcomes.description: Explain step-growth, chain-growth and copolymerization mechanisms and calculate elementary conversion relationships.
Calculate molecular-weight averages and interpret size-exclusion, thermal and spectroscopic characterization.
Relate architecture, crystallinity and crosslinking to thermal, mechanical and recycling behavior.

practice: Analyze molecular-weight distributions and select polymerization and characterization strategies for specified properties.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Materials Chemistry

outcomes.description: Analyze crystal stoichiometry, coordination, defects and phase stability in inorganic solids.
Choose solid-state, solution, vapor and sol-gel synthesis routes using kinetic and processing constraints.
Interpret powder diffraction and complementary composition data to connect structure with material function.

practice: Design a benign solid preparation and index supplied diffraction patterns with phase and defect checks.

includes: Proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Biomolecular Chemistry

outcomes.description: Represent major biomolecule classes and relate covalent structure to chemical function.
Explain folding, assembly and ligand binding and calculate elementary occupancy and acid-base effects.
Explain catalytic strategies and interpret enzyme saturation and inhibition using explicitly specified algebraic models.

practice: Interpret molecular structures and binding curves and propose chemical explanations for mutational effects.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Metabolic Biochemistry

outcomes.description: Trace atoms, reducing equivalents and intermediates through central carbon and major biosynthetic pathways.
Calculate ATP and redox balances using locally defined free-energy and electrochemical-gradient relationships.
Predict pathway responses to regulation, enzyme inhibition and nutritional changes using kinetic reasoning.

practice: Solve isotope-tracing and energy-accounting problems and interpret metabolic perturbation datasets.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry

outcomes.description: Predict acid-base, redox and partitioning controls on chemicals in air, water and soils.
Construct and solve bounded compartment and first-order fate models with mass-balance checks.
Evaluate monitoring and remediation choices using chemical persistence, exposure, uncertainty and environmental justice.

practice: Analyze a supplied contamination case and defend sampling, fate estimates and remediation priorities.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Computational Chemistry

outcomes.description: Execute and diagnose electronic-structure calculations, geometry optimization and basis or method convergence.
Implement elementary molecular dynamics and Metropolis sampling and interpret ensemble and finite-size effects.
Validate predicted energies, structures and observables against reference data with uncertainty and provenance.

practice: Run documented electronic calculations and implement a small molecular sampler with convergence diagnostics.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Molecular and network theories of reaction rates.
decks.title: Reaction Dynamics

outcomes.description: Derive transition-state rate expressions and evaluate partition, tunneling and recrossing corrections.
Analyze collision, reaction-coordinate and energy-transfer models under explicit approximations.
Construct coupled kinetic equations and assess parameter identifiability and competing mechanisms from time-series data.

practice: Derive rate predictions and use a supplied ODE-fitting tool with explicit residual and identifiability checks.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Process Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive mass and energy balances for batch, stirred-tank and plug-flow reactors and identify runaway conditions.
Calculate elementary equilibrium-stage distillation and extraction designs and material recycles.
Compare process routes using hazard analysis, atom economy, waste, energy and lifecycle boundaries.

practice: Design a bounded reactor-separator flowsheet and submit balances, sensitivity studies and a hazard review.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Medicinal Chemistry and Chemical Biology

outcomes.description: Design interpretable analogue series and distinguish binding, functional potency and selectivity evidence.
Evaluate solubility, permeability, metabolism and toxicity tradeoffs using bounded pharmacochemical models.
Design orthogonal controls that detect assay interference, off-target action and invalid chemical-probe claims.

practice: Critique an assay package and propose a synthesizable analogue series with explicit decision criteria.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Advanced integration of molecular and interfacial catalysis.
decks.title: Catalysis Research

outcomes.description: Construct catalytic microkinetic models incorporating coverage, competing pathways and deactivation.
Design kinetic and operando evidence that distinguishes active-site, transport and restructuring explanations.

practice: Develop and defend a catalyst-mechanism research proposal with falsifiable alternatives and quantitative predictions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Living Systems

outcomes.description: Explain cells, organisms and ecosystems as open systems using matter, energy and information models.
Distinguish major lineages, organizational scales and reproductive life histories using observable characteristics.
Distinguish experimental and historical evidence and explain common ancestry and natural selection conceptually.

practice: Compare organisms and biological explanations using observations, diagrams and evidence-based written arguments.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Observation Methods

outcomes.description: Use microscope images and calibration scales to identify structures and estimate dimensions.
Collect standardized observations and distinguish sampling units, artifacts and repeated measurements.
Document specimens and observations and justify basic containment, handling and disposal choices.

practice: Prepare or inspect benign specimens and maintain illustrated, traceable observation records.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology

outcomes.description: Relate organelles, cytoskeleton and basic macromolecular roles to cellular organization and energy use.
Explain diffusion, osmosis and active transport using concentration, permeability and electrochemical models.
Trace receptor signaling, cell-cycle control and apoptosis and predict elementary perturbation effects.

practice: Interpret cell images and perturbation experiments; construct transport and signaling diagrams.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics

outcomes.description: Predict inheritance outcomes for autosomal, sex-linked, cytoplasmic and interacting loci.
Infer linkage and genetic-map distances from crosses while recognizing recombination limits.
Interpret penetrance, expressivity, environmental effects and chromosome abnormalities in genotype-phenotype claims.

practice: Solve pedigree and cross problems and critique deterministic interpretations of genetic results.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology

outcomes.description: Distinguish selection, drift, mutation and migration and calculate elementary Hardy-Weinberg and selection examples.
Evaluate adaptation and speciation hypotheses using variation, reproductive isolation and alternative explanations.
Interpret homology, phylogenetic trees and fossil or biogeographic evidence without ladder-like progress assumptions.

practice: Analyze evolutionary case studies and construct competing explanations with discriminating evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology

outcomes.description: Interpret discrete growth, competition, predation and food-web models using graphs and simple recurrences.
Construct matter and energy budgets and explain productivity and nutrient cycling.
Explain niche, disturbance, succession and spatial heterogeneity across ecological scales.

practice: Build food webs and ecosystem budgets; compare ecological explanations using supplied field observations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Research Methods

outcomes.description: Design controlled biological studies with appropriate units, replication, randomization and blinding.
Analyze biological measurements with justified tests, effect sizes and sensitivity to missingness or batch effects.
Resolve research cases involving consent, animal welfare, provenance, data sharing and dual-use concerns.

practice: Write a preregistered benign study and analyze supplied data with an ethical and reproducibility review.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Biology

outcomes.description: Explain replication, repair, transcription and translation and predict consequences of molecular perturbations.
Design and interpret extraction, electrophoresis, PCR, hybridization and sequencing assays with appropriate controls.
Analyze prokaryotic and eukaryotic gene-regulatory logic using expression and perturbation evidence.

practice: Design primer and control logic using supplied sequences; interpret gels and expression experiments.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology

outcomes.description: Compare cellular microbial lineages, structures and metabolic strategies.
Calculate growth and viable counts and explain nutrient, environmental and antimicrobial effects.
Select and interpret culture, staining, biochemical and susceptibility assays with contamination controls.

practice: Use approved nonpathogenic cultures or supplied images and growth data to identify and quantify microbes.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Botany

outcomes.description: Relate plant tissues and organs to growth, support, transport and resource capture.
Compare alternation of generations, reproductive structures and seed or fruit development.
Use diagnostic traits and keys to identify major plant groups and infer structural homologies.

practice: Construct annotated plant specimens or image portfolios and apply identification keys.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Zoology

outcomes.description: Compare symmetry, segmentation, cavities and developmental organization across animal body plans.
Relate comparative feeding, locomotor, respiratory and reproductive structures to ecological demands.
Use morphological keys and comparative evidence to identify major animal groups.

practice: Analyze specimens or approved digital anatomy resources and construct comparative character matrices.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Organ systems as regulated biological processes.
decks.title: Animal and Human Physiology

outcomes.description: Construct feedback models and explain set points, gain, compensation and homeostatic failure.
Calculate bounded flow, gas-exchange, filtration and balance models and interpret organ-system integration.
Explain endocrine, digestive and reproductive regulation and predict responses to physiological perturbations.

practice: Analyze supplied physiological traces and balance problems; compare normal compensation with specified dysfunction.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience

outcomes.description: Explain membrane potentials, action potentials and synaptic integration using explicitly defined conductance models.
Trace sensory coding and motor-control pathways and predict consequences of localized lesions.
Evaluate plasticity, learning and cognitive hypotheses using behavioral, recording and intervention evidence.

practice: Interpret neural recordings and lesion cases; distinguish correlational signals from causal neural evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology

outcomes.description: Explain axis formation, positional information and patterning through signaling and gene-regulatory interactions.
Relate cell differentiation, migration, adhesion and programmed death to morphogenesis and regeneration.
Design lineage-tracing, transplantation and perturbation tests that distinguish developmental mechanisms.

practice: Interpret fate maps and perturbation series and construct testable developmental mechanism diagrams.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology

outcomes.description: Explain innate sensing, antigen presentation and receptor diversification in immune recognition.
Trace cellular and humoral responses, memory and vaccination and interpret standard immune assays.
Distinguish mechanisms of immunodeficiency, hypersensitivity, autoimmunity and transplant rejection.

practice: Interpret flow diagrams and supplied serological data; explain contrasting immune-pathology cases.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Virology

outcomes.description: Compare viral entry, genome replication, expression, assembly and release strategies.
Explain host range, persistence, immune evasion and viral evolutionary change.
Interpret plaque, infectivity, antigen and nucleic-acid assays while distinguishing detection from infectious potential.

practice: Analyze supplied viral-assay and sequence cases; design non-executed control and interpretation plans.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecological Methods

outcomes.description: Design quadrat, transect and stratified surveys accounting for scale, detection and spatial dependence.
Estimate abundance, survival and recruitment from life tables and elementary mark-recapture models.
Calculate diversity and dissimilarity and interpret ordination and community comparisons using supplied software.

practice: Design a permitted field survey and analyze supplied detection, life-table and community datasets.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecological Dynamics

outcomes.description: Construct continuous and stage-structured population models and calculate equilibria and growth sensitivity.
Analyze competition, consumer-resource and food-web models using Jacobians and stability criteria.
Analyze patch, dispersal and metapopulation models and connect parameters to ecological measurements.

practice: Derive and compare population models using phase portraits, eigenvalues and supplied numerical solvers.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Population Genetics

outcomes.description: Derive allele-frequency recursions and analyze selection, migration, mutation and linkage equilibria.
Calculate drift, fixation and elementary coalescent quantities and interpret genetic-diversity evidence.
Partition quantitative genetic variance and predict selection response while distinguishing heritability from causation.

practice: Derive genetic models and analyze allele-frequency and pedigree datasets with explicit assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Phylogenetics and Comparative Methods

outcomes.description: Construct character matrices and compare distance, parsimony and likelihood tree methods using taught substitution models.
Interpret bootstrap, likelihood and posterior tree support and diagnose alignment or model artifacts.
Apply independent-contrast and phylogenetic-regression models using supplied software and assess evolutionary assumptions.

practice: Reconstruct trees with documented tools and compare trait conclusions across trees and evolutionary models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation Biology

outcomes.description: Assess extinction risk using habitat, demographic, genetic and uncertainty evidence.
Compare protected-area, restoration, harvest and invasive-species interventions using explicit monitoring criteria.
Evaluate conservation tradeoffs involving local rights, Indigenous knowledge, animal welfare and distributional effects.

practice: Produce a conservation decision dossier with alternative actions, uncertainty and stakeholder reasoning.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Behavioral Biology

outcomes.description: Construct ethograms and reliable sampling schemes controlling observer effects and nonindependence.
Distinguish developmental, physiological and environmental mechanisms of learning, communication and behavior.
Evaluate foraging, mating, cooperation and conflict hypotheses using explicit fitness and alternative-explanation models.

practice: Score approved behavioral recordings and compare proximate and ultimate explanations with uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics

outcomes.description: Parse sequence formats and use documented alignment and database tools with scoring and homology checks.
Execute read-quality, mapping and variant workflows and diagnose coverage, reference and batch artifacts.
Analyze expression and enrichment using count models, multiplicity control and biologically appropriate contrasts.

practice: Build versioned sequence and omics workflows using supplied aligners; document quality checks and interpretation limits.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biotechnology

outcomes.description: Design cloning, expression and genome-editing strategies with explicit sequence, delivery and control logic.
Plan molecular and phenotypic validation that distinguishes intended changes from off-target or contextual effects.
Evaluate containment, consent, ownership, ecological impact and dual-use tradeoffs in biotechnology cases.

practice: Design a benign, non-executed engineering project or approved teaching experiment with validation and governance plans.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Cell and Molecular Biology

outcomes.description: Design imaging, fractionation and perturbation experiments that distinguish competing cellular mechanisms.
Explain trafficking, cytoskeletal assembly and mechanochemical organization using molecular interaction evidence.
Infer chromatin, RNA-processing and regulatory mechanisms from orthogonal perturbation and molecular assays.

practice: Reconstruct a mechanistic paper and design orthogonal experiments capable of falsifying its central model.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems Biology

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric and kinetic models and analyze conservation, equilibria and feedback.
Estimate network parameters using supplied solvers and assess sensitivity, identifiability and predictive uncertainty.
Design perturbations and constrained flux analyses that distinguish competing network explanations.

practice: Build a small regulatory or metabolic model and defend parameter inference and perturbation selection.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Physiology

outcomes.description: Calculate water-potential and transport relationships and interpret stomatal and phloem regulation.
Analyze photosynthetic light and carbon responses using gas-exchange and fluorescence measurements.
Explain hormonal, photoperiodic and stress responses and design discriminating plant experiments.

practice: Analyze plant water-status and photosynthesis datasets and design a controlled environmental-response study.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Pathobiology

outcomes.description: Explain pathogen invasion, host damage and resistance using microbial, viral and immune mechanisms.
Analyze oncogenic and inherited disease mechanisms from genotype through cellular and organ phenotypes.
Distinguish mechanisms of injury, repair, metabolic dysfunction and degeneration using mechanistic evidence.

practice: Analyze nonclinical mechanism cases and propose experiments distinguishing competing disease explanations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Epidemiology and Public Health

outcomes.description: Calculate incidence, prevalence, risk ratios, odds ratios and screening performance with appropriate denominators.
Compare cohort, case-control and trial designs using causal diagrams, bias and confounding analysis.
Interpret surveillance and outbreak evidence and evaluate interventions, equity and communication under uncertainty.

practice: Analyze supplied public-health datasets and produce a causal critique and intervention decision brief.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Paleobiology

outcomes.description: Combine fossil identification, stratigraphic ordering and locally taught radiometric-decay calculations to infer relative and absolute time.
Evaluate preservation, reworking and collection biases in fossil assemblages.
Compare diversification, extinction and morphological-change hypotheses using fossil and living-organism evidence.

practice: Interpret stratigraphic sections and fossil datasets and quantify how alternative preservation models change conclusions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Microbial communities as ecological and metabolic systems.
decks.title: Microbial Ecology

outcomes.description: Infer microbial community structure and function while diagnosing compositional, extraction and annotation biases.
Design isotope, activity and environmental-gradient measurements linking microbial populations to biogeochemical rates.

practice: Analyze paired metagenomic and process datasets and propose experiments separating abundance from activity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Synthetic Biology

outcomes.description: Design and quantitatively compare bounded synthetic regulatory or metabolic networks under resource constraints.
Predict mutation, selection and burden-driven failure modes and propose stability tests.
Construct an assurance case integrating controls, containment, monitoring and responsible deployment boundaries.

practice: Develop a non-deployment design dossier with quantitative predictions, evolutionary failure tests and containment reasoning.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Digital Foundations

outcomes.description: Encode and decode binary integers, text and sampled media and explain precision and compression tradeoffs.
Explain algorithms, stored programs, hardware-software interfaces and networked computation using concrete system diagrams.

practice: Trace small encoded messages and explain the components involved in storing, executing and transmitting them.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Foundations

outcomes.description: Write structured programs using variables, conditionals, loops, functions and elementary recursion.
Process strings, lists, mappings and structured files with explicit input validation.
Develop tests and use tracing and debugging tools to locate and correct program defects.

practice: Implement small data-processing programs from specifications and submit tests, debugging records and readable code.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Data Structures

outcomes.description: Implement lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, trees and heaps and preserve representation invariants.
Specify abstract interfaces and choose representations based on required operations and failure cases.
Calculate elementary time and space costs using operation counts and asymptotic notation.

practice: Implement and test competing collection representations and benchmark adversarial as well as typical inputs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Algorithms

outcomes.description: Design divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic-programming algorithms and derive their recurrences.
Implement traversal, shortest-path, spanning-tree and network-flow algorithms with suitable representations.
Prove algorithm correctness and asymptotic bounds, including amortized and elementary lower-bound arguments.

practice: Implement algorithms, prove invariants and compare theoretical bounds with measured adversarial performance.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Architecture

outcomes.description: Construct combinational and sequential logic circuits from Boolean and state-machine specifications.
Trace instruction execution and design a small datapath with control and pipelining.
Calculate cache, locality and pipeline effects and diagnose architectural performance bottlenecks.

practice: Use a taught logic simulator and assembly environment to build and benchmark a small processor model.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Systems Programming

outcomes.description: Write low-level programs with explicit memory layout, pointer validity and resource-lifetime management.
Implement binary serialization and file or process interactions using documented system-call interfaces.
Diagnose memory corruption, undefined behavior and interface defects using debuggers and sanitizers.

practice: Implement binary utilities and resource-safe system programs; submit sanitizer and debugger evidence.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems

outcomes.description: Implement and reason about scheduling, synchronization and deadlock in process and thread models.
Trace address translation and analyze paging, allocation and replacement policies.
Analyze filesystem consistency, access control and kernel isolation under faults and concurrent use.

practice: Modify a teaching kernel or simulator and test synchronization, paging and storage failure cases.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks

outcomes.description: Trace encapsulation, addressing and naming across link, network, transport and application layers.
Execute routing and reliable-delivery algorithms and calculate delay, throughput and congestion effects.
Write bounded socket applications and interpret packet captures using locally taught interfaces and tools.

practice: Build an isolated client-server application and analyze packet traces under loss, delay and malformed inputs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Databases

outcomes.description: Design relational schemas using keys, dependencies and normalization while preserving application meaning.
Write relational algebra and SQL and analyze index and join execution strategies.
Explain isolation, serializability, logging and recovery and diagnose transactional anomalies.

practice: Build and query a database; compare query plans and reproduce transaction anomalies in a sandbox.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Engineering maintainable software beyond individual coding.
decks.title: Software Engineering

outcomes.description: Translate stakeholder needs into testable requirements and modular designs with explicit tradeoffs.
Design unit, integration and property-based tests and conduct actionable code reviews.
Use version control, continuous integration and issue tracking to manage changes and technical debt.

practice: Deliver a small team project with reviewed changes, automated tests and documented requirement traceability.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Human-centered design with an accessible entry.
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction

outcomes.description: Conduct consent-aware interviews and task analysis and derive defensible user requirements.
Construct interactive prototypes using accessibility, feedback and cognitive-load principles.
Plan and interpret think-aloud and heuristic evaluations and distinguish evidence from designer preference.

practice: Prototype an accessible interface and conduct an approved small usability study with a revision rationale.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Theory of Computation

outcomes.description: Construct automata and grammars and prove closure, equivalence and nonrecognizability results.
Formalize computation with machines and prove decidability or undecidability using reductions and diagonalization.

practice: Construct recognizers and write reduction proofs, including explicit encodings and correctness arguments.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computational Complexity

outcomes.description: Prove completeness results using polynomial reductions and distinguish decision, search and optimization formulations.
Analyze approximation guarantees and randomized algorithms using explicit probability and resource bounds.
Prove representative space, hierarchy and relativization results and distinguish established separations from open conjectures.

practice: Write complete reductions and resource proofs and construct algorithms meeting stated approximation contracts.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Languages

outcomes.description: Specify and compare small-step and big-step semantics for representative language constructs.
Construct type derivations and prove progress and preservation for a small typed language.
Implement interpreters with lexical scope, closures and multiple evaluation strategies.

practice: Implement a small interpreter and prove selected semantic and type-safety properties.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compilers

outcomes.description: Construct lexical and parsing stages and resolve grammar ambiguity with explicit language specifications.
Lower typed programs through intermediate representations to machine-level code with correct calling conventions.
Implement data-flow analyses and optimizations and justify semantic preservation conditions.

practice: Build a small compiler and use differential testing plus semantic arguments to validate transformations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Accessible security reasoning before specialized systems theory.
decks.title: Security Foundations

outcomes.description: Construct threat models identifying assets, adversaries, trust boundaries and misuse cases.
Choose authentication, authorization and established cryptographic interfaces without confusing their security guarantees.
Explain injection, unsafe input handling and session failures using bounded application models and defenses.

practice: Threat-model a teaching application and repair intentionally vulnerable examples in an isolated authorized environment.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Cryptography

outcomes.description: State indistinguishability and unforgeability experiments and construct elementary reduction arguments.
Analyze encryption, authentication, signatures and key exchange under explicit number-theoretic or pseudorandomness assumptions.
Diagnose nonce, randomness and composition failures and design bounded authenticated protocols.

practice: Write security reductions and demonstrate toy construction failures without deploying homemade cryptography.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Systems and Network Security

outcomes.description: Design least-privilege, isolation and defense-in-depth controls across hosts and network services.
Conduct scoped code, configuration and network assessments and validate remediations with reproducible tests.
Reconstruct incidents from logs and artifacts and justify containment, evidence preservation and disclosure decisions.

practice: Assess an isolated teaching service, implement defenses and produce an evidence-preserving incident report.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Computation under concurrency and partial failure.
decks.title: Distributed Systems

outcomes.description: Reason about logical clocks, causality, consistency and partial-failure assumptions.
Explain and implement bounded replication and consensus protocols and justify safety and liveness conditions.
Build a distributed service and diagnose partitions, retries, duplicate effects and recovery behavior.

practice: Implement a replicated teaching service and test protocol invariants under injected failures and message schedules.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Parallel Computing

outcomes.description: Design parallel reductions, scans, sorting and decomposition strategies with work-span analysis.
Implement shared-memory, message-passing and accelerator kernels with explicit synchronization and memory semantics.
Measure speedup, communication and locality costs and diagnose race and scalability failures.

practice: Implement parallel array and graph kernels and report correctness, race checks and scaling measurements.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Artificial Intelligence

outcomes.description: Implement heuristic search, constraint satisfaction and classical planning and analyze their failure modes.
Represent knowledge in logical rules and implement sound bounded inference procedures.
Construct finite probabilistic and utility models and calculate elementary decisions under uncertainty.

practice: Implement search and rule-based agents and compare their behavior under incomplete or misspecified models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Working learning algorithms and empirical discipline.
decks.title: Machine Learning

outcomes.description: Implement linear, tree, nearest-neighbor and kernel-based learners and compare inductive biases and regularization.
Implement clustering and principal-component methods and evaluate representation and distance assumptions.
Design leakage-resistant validation and evaluate calibration, imbalance, subgroup performance and distribution mismatch.

practice: Implement representative learners and submit reproducible model comparisons with held-out and subgroup diagnostics.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Deep Learning

outcomes.description: Derive backpropagation and implement reverse-mode differentiation for a small computational graph.
Construct convolutional, recurrent and attention-based networks and explain their representational assumptions.
Diagnose optimization, normalization, overfitting and numerical failures through controlled training experiments.

practice: Implement a small autodifferentiation engine and train controlled neural baselines with ablation studies.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Probabilistic Artificial Intelligence

outcomes.description: Construct directed and undirected graphical models and derive factorization and conditional-independence properties.
Implement variable elimination, message passing, Monte Carlo and variational inference with diagnostics.
Derive and implement expectation-maximization and compare latent-model identifiability and predictive uncertainty.

practice: Implement inference on a common graphical model and compare exact, sampling and variational results.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Reinforcement Learning

outcomes.description: Derive Bellman equations and implement finite-state value and policy iteration.
Implement temporal-difference, action-value and policy-gradient methods and state their convergence assumptions.
Evaluate exploration, reward specification and off-policy estimates under safety and distribution constraints.

practice: Implement agents in bounded simulators and compare learning curves, uncertainty and reward-induced failure cases.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Graphics

outcomes.description: Implement coordinate transformations, camera projections and geometric interpolation using homogeneous coordinates.
Implement triangle rasterization, clipping and depth-based visibility with sampling diagnostics.
Implement elementary ray intersections, reflection and shading models and explain their physical approximations.

practice: Build a small rasterizer and ray tracer and compare images under controlled geometric and sampling changes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Vision

outcomes.description: Model image formation and implement spatial and frequency filters with noise and sampling analysis.
Estimate camera geometry, correspondences and elementary three-dimensional structure with robust fitting.
Construct recognition and segmentation pipelines and assess localization, domain and subgroup errors.

practice: Implement filtering and geometric reconstruction and evaluate a recognition pipeline on controlled distribution shifts.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics

outcomes.description: Derive rigid-transform kinematics, Jacobians and inverse-kinematic solutions for elementary robots.
Implement Bayesian filtering and elementary localization with explicit sensor and motion uncertainty models.
Implement collision-aware planning and integrate feedback control while diagnosing model and actuation limits.

practice: Implement a simulated robot with localization, planning and control; test sensor faults and collision constraints.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Methods

outcomes.description: Specify contracts and prove partial and total correctness using invariants and locally taught proof-assistant workflows.
Construct transition models and verify temporal properties using explicit and symbolic model-checking procedures.
Evaluate abstraction soundness, specification gaps and trusted components in verification assurance claims.

practice: Submit a machine-checked program proof and a model-checking study with explicit specification limitations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Information Theory

outcomes.description: Calculate entropy, divergence and mutual information and prove elementary information inequalities.
Construct prefix codes and derive source-coding bounds using typicality and Kraft-type arguments.
Calculate discrete channel capacity in elementary cases and explain random-coding and converse arguments.

practice: Construct codes and prove rate bounds; calculate communication limits for explicit finite channels.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Natural Language Processing

outcomes.description: Compare tokenization, morphology, syntax and semantic representations and diagnose multilingual representation failures.
Implement sequence decoding and train bounded language or sequence-labeling models with appropriate objectives.
Evaluate generation and understanding using task metrics, human judgments, factuality and bias analyses.

practice: Build a small language pipeline and compare automatic metrics with consent-aware human error analysis.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Reliable large-scale data movement and transformation.
decks.title: Data Engineering

outcomes.description: Design reproducible ingestion and transformation pipelines with schema evolution and idempotent recovery.
Implement validation, lineage and access controls and diagnose data-contract and provenance failures.
Implement windowed stream processing and reason about event time, late data and delivery semantics.

practice: Build a versioned batch-and-stream pipeline and test schema changes, duplicates, delayed events and recovery.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Established ethical and societal computing competence.
decks.title: Computing, Ethics and Society

outcomes.description: Analyze how computing systems redistribute power, privacy, access, labor and environmental burdens.
Justify professional decisions concerning consent, intellectual property, disclosure, accessibility and conflicts of interest.
Compare elementary fairness measures and construct accountability plans with contestability and stakeholder participation.

practice: Write contrasting stakeholder analyses and defend a professional decision using explicit ethical arguments and evidence.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Quantum Computing

outcomes.description: Construct and simulate quantum circuits and calculate measurement and entanglement behavior.
Derive elementary query, Fourier and amplitude-amplification algorithms and compare resource claims.
Analyze elementary noise channels and demonstrate detection and correction with simple quantum codes.

practice: Implement a small state-vector simulator and compare ideal and noisy algorithm and code behavior.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Reliable Machine Learning

outcomes.description: Design shift and robustness experiments that separate sampling error, adaptation and model misspecification.
Derive and test bounded calibration or conformal guarantees and identify assumption-breaking cases.
Construct auditable learning-system assurance cases integrating statistical evidence, subgroup harms and deployment limits.

practice: Reproduce and challenge a reliability claim with shifted data, uncertainty diagnostics and a stakeholder-aware audit.
